answers.answer: 1. Select 3 Escape Pods in a four-player game. 2. Place the lowest-numbered selected Pod in Section A, the next in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up. 3. The Intruder bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, and 3 Adults plus 1 Adult per player (7 Adults for four players).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 7 and 10: 3 Pods for 3–4 players; lowest number in A, next in B, alternate; all Locked; bag contents listed.

answers.answer: 1. Remove Corporate and Personal Objective cards marked for more players than are in the game, shuffle the decks separately, and deal each player one of each before the Character draft. 2. At the First Encounter—when the first Intruder miniature appears—each player chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the rejected card from the game face down, unseen by anyone. 3. Eggs do not trigger this choice because they are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: Setup step 16; Critical gameplay moments: First Encounter; Eggs do not trigger it.

answers.answer: 1. Discard the Action card being played and 2 additional Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2. 2. Do not discard either Contamination card for payment; Contamination cards cannot pay Action costs. 3. If the card has sections separated by OR, choose one section/effect; the cost remains the card plus the required additional Action cards.
answers.evidence: Actions: an Action card is discarded plus the required additional cards; Contamination cannot pay; OR means choose one.

answers.answer: 1. They take 1 Light Wound at the end of their own round, after taking their one Action and passing. 2. Once passed, they cannot take further normal Actions that Player Phase, though the FAQ permits Interruption after passing. 3. When passing, they may discard any number of cards from their hand. 4. Later players' rounds do not cause this Character to take Fire damage again that turn; Fire damage is assessed when that Character ends their own round.
answers.evidence: Player rounds: one Action means pass; passing ends normal Actions and allows discarding; Fire wound applies at the end of that Character's round.

answers.answer: 1. On entering the empty unexplored Room, flip its tile face up, reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return the token to the box. Set the Room's Item count by rotating the tile until the token's number faces the board's Item Counter; do not set a count for the Nest or Slime Room. 2. Resolve the token effect: Silence means no Noise roll; Danger means no Noise roll and moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room, or, if none are eligible, places Noise in each connected Corridor without a marker. Other effects place Slime, Fire, Malfunction, or a Door as indicated. 3. If the destination is empty and the effect does not replace the roll, roll Noise: 1–4 places a marker in the corresponding Corridor (a marker already there causes an Encounter); Danger resolves as above; Silence places none. Slime turns Silence into Danger. 4. If a Character or Intruder is already in the destination Room, do not roll Noise.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll.

answers.answer: 1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination; it also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results. 2. It follows normal movement restrictions, cannot be used in Combat, and is forbidden if every Corridor connected to the destination already has Noise. 3. A Closed Door blocks movement through that Corridor. 4. A miniature may never stop in a Corridor; it must end in a Room.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions: Careful Movement; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors: Closed Door blocks neighboring status and no one stops in Corridors.

answers.answer: 1. Because that Corridor already has Noise, placing another marker there causes an Encounter. First discard all Noise in Corridors connected to the Room, including the Technical Corridors space if connected. 2. Draw an Intruder token and place the matching miniature; keep a drawn non-Blank token outside the bag until a rule returns it (for example, hiding in Technical Corridors). 3. Compare its number with the triggering player's hand size, counting both Action and Contamination cards. Fewer cards than the token number causes a Surprise Attack against that Character. 4. Contamination cards count for this comparison, though they cannot pay Action costs.
answers.evidence: Noise roll: an existing marker causes Encounter; Encounters: clear connected Noise, draw/place, compare number to Action and Contamination cards, and set non-Blank token aside.

answers.answer: 1. On Danger, move all Intruders in neighboring Rooms that are not in Combat with any Character into the destination Room. 2. If there are no eligible neighboring Intruders (including when all are in Combat), place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one, including Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance. 3. An Intruder moving into a Character's Room is not an Encounter; it simply puts them in Combat. 4. Slime makes a Silence result resolve as Danger.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens: Danger; Encounters: movement into a Character's Room is not an Encounter; Slime and Noise markers.

answers.answer: 1. In an Encounter, a Blank causes a Noise marker to be placed in each Corridor connected to that Room, returns to the bag, and no Intruder miniature appears. 2. Add an Adult token only if that Blank was the last token in the bag, and only if an Adult token is available. 3. In bag development, a Blank adds an Adult if one is available regardless of whether it was the last token; then the Blank returns to the bag.
answers.evidence: Encounters: Blank token; Event Phase, Intruder bag development: Blank.

answers.answer: 1. Both Intruders fail to move through the same Closed Door: they destroy it simultaneously and stay in their originating Room. The Door token lies down to show Destroyed. 2. A Destroyed Door cannot later be Closed again, except by the Plasma Torch Item. 3. A Noise-triggered Intruder appearance through a Corridor with a Closed Door is not blocked; it appears regardless of the Door.
answers.evidence: Door tokens: several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy the Door simultaneously and stay; destroyed doors cannot be closed except with Plasma Torch; Noise appearance ignores a Closed Door.

answers.answer: 1. When an Intruder enters a Technical Corridors Entrance, remove its miniature, discard all Injury markers, and return its token to the Intruder bag. 2. Noise already on the Technical Corridors space remains there. 3. Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors (except the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action card and Technical Corridor Plans Item), and Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors: Intruder hiding; Characters' exceptions; Door tokens and Noise.

answers.answer: 1. Both Shoot and Melee are Actions with a cost of 1 Action card. For Shoot, choose a Weapon in Hand and an Intruder in your Room, discard 1 Ammo from that Weapon, and roll the Combat die; a miss has no Melee penalty. 2. For Melee, draw a Contamination card onto your Action discard pile, choose an Intruder in your Room, and roll the die; a miss gives you 1 Serious Wound. 3. In Melee, a die result that would deal 2 Injuries deals only 1 Injury.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions and Combat: Shoot and Melee procedures; double-hit result in Melee counts as one.

answers.answer: 1. After Injury markers are added, check against the Intruder's current total injuries. A Larva dies at 1 Injury. 2. An Adult draws one Intruder Attack card for its blood value; blood less than or equal to its injuries kills it. 3. A Queen draws two cards and sums their blood values; a sum less than or equal to its injuries kills it. Adult and Queen deaths remove the miniature and place an Intruder Carcass in the Room; Larvae leave no Carcass. 4. If a Queen's injury check draws a Retreat arrow on either card, it retreats instead of resolving the numerical death check: draw an Event card and move it through the Corridor matching the card's Intruder movement number.
answers.evidence: Combat: Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat.

answers.answer: 1. Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack for each of the two Intruders, starting with the larger types (Queen, Breeder, Adult, then Larva). Escape attacks target the escaping Character. 2. If the Character dies, their Corpse remains in the Room they tried to leave. 3. If they survive, they complete the move to the neighboring Room; because it is unexplored, reveal and resolve its Exploration token, and because it is empty, roll Noise unless the exploration effect replaces that roll.
answers.evidence: Combat: Character Escape; Movement and Exploration tokens.

answers.answer: 1. With several Characters in the Room, the Intruder targets the one whose player has the fewest Action cards; ties go to the Character with the First Player token or next in turn order. 2. Draw one Intruder Attack card: a matching Intruder symbol is a hit and its effect resolves; otherwise it misses. 3. A Larva does not draw an Attack card: remove it from the board, put it on the target's Character board, and give the target a Contamination card on top of their Action discard pile. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears and the target still gains Contamination, but is not automatically killed.
answers.evidence: Intruder Attack and Infest (Larva attack); Contamination cards: placement on Action discard pile.

answers.answer: 1. Dressing one of three Serious Wounds does not prevent death from any further Wound, including a Light Wound. 2. Otherwise, a third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound, as the healing effect specifies. 4. On death, place a Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death; FAQ: Heavy Objects drop in the Room on death.

answers.answer: 1. Canteen and Shower scan only Contamination cards in the user's hand; remove all non-Infected cards. If an Infected card is found, put a Larva on the Character board; if one is already there, the Character dies and a Creeper appears in the Room. Canteen also heals 1 Light Wound; Shower removes Slime. 2. Surgery scans Contamination cards in the deck, hand, and discard pile and removes all Infected cards; it also removes a Larva if present. It costs 2 Action cards, causes 1 Light Wound, and automatically passes. Shuffle the Character's entire hand and all remaining cards, including remaining Contamination, into the Action deck; the hand remains empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: Room Actions: Canteen, Surgery, Shower; Contamination and Infection.

answers.answer: 1. In a Room with uncarried Eggs, Shoot or Melee attacks can target them; each Injury destroys one Egg. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Serious Wound. The summary says the manual does not settle whether a successful Egg Melee gives Contamination. 2. A Grenade destroys 2 uncarried Eggs and a Molotov Cocktail destroys 1; they may be thrown at a Room with Eggs as if an Intruder were there. 3. After every individual attempt to destroy an Egg, roll Noise. If throwing at Nest Eggs from another Room, roll Noise in the thrower's Room. 4. During each Fire Damage step, Fire in a Room with uncarried Eggs destroys 1 Egg. When no Eggs remain in the Nest, the Nest is destroyed and marked with an Injury marker.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest; FAQ Rooms 2: Noise from thrown explosives is rolled in the thrower's Room; successful Egg Melee contamination is expressly unresolved.

answers.answer: 1. To enter, use the matching Evacuation Section A/B Room Action (cost 2 Action cards); its Pod must be Unlocked and have room, and the Section must contain neither an Intruder nor a Malfunction. Roll Noise first; if an Intruder appears or is present in the Section, entry fails. 2. Each Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use Hand slots and take no Character space. 3. If you launch after boarding, remove the Pod and occupants from play; they still face Contamination and Objective checks. If you wait, you pass the current turn and remain present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls. In each later Player Phase, at the start of your first round choose to keep waiting and pass, launch, or exit for free into the Section Room and take a full round of 2 Actions. A second Character boarding may launch the Pod immediately with both aboard. If an Intruder appears in the Section while you wait, Pod occupants return to the Room. A Malfunction while waiting does not prevent waiting, launching, or exiting, but prevents new Pod entry.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods: Board, Capacity, Launch immediately, Wait after boarding, second Character, Intruder and Malfunction while waiting.

answers.answer: 1. The Victory Check order is Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, then Objectives. 2. If 2 or 3 Engines are Damaged, the ship explodes and everyone aboard—including hibernating Characters and Intruders—dies; launched Pod passengers are already away. 3. If the destination is not Earth, all hibernating Characters die, except a Character with the Quarantine Objective if the destination is Mars. 4. Each survivor, including Pod passengers, checks Contamination. Scan cards in deck, discard, and hand; if any is Infected, shuffle all cards and draw 4, and any Contamination card among those four kills the Character. A Character carrying a Larva skips the initial Scan and takes the same shuffle-and-draw-four test. Without a Larva or an Infected card, no four-card test is required.
answers.evidence: Victory Check: Engines, Coordinates, Contamination; Escape Pods: launched occupants still face final Contamination and Objective checks.
